relevance.rationale: Same broad theme — knotted/linked QCD flux tubes as physical objects — but, as read, it supplies nothing this folio can consume. Its actual content is cosmological: a tightly knotted flux-tube network formed at a QCD-like transition acts as an effective cosmological constant and drives inflation, and since 1-dimensional knots are topologically stable only in three space dimensions this is offered as an explanation for d=3. QOU has no cosmology and no inflation sector, and its d=3 appears only as an input assumption to the Navier-Stokes universality argument (p4-universality.md), not as something the folio derives or wants to derive. The one adjacent QOU object — the glueball as the simplest non-trivial closed vortex (models-of-qous/yang-mills-mass-gap.md) — is served by the Buniy-Kephart knotted-glueball work that this paper merely cites as its ref [5], not by this paper. This is a scope-(a) negative: this document, as read, supplies nothing usable here; it does not exclude the knotted-flux-tube picture as a source of prior art.

proposedActions.rationale: No key result maps onto a named QOU block. If prior art for the knotted-flux-tube hadron picture is later wanted (the avrin-2012 precedent), the correct source is the Buniy-Kephart glueball paper this one cites, not this cosmology paper.
